verdict: Oracle's revenue grew 12% to $14.9B as cloud revenue jumped 28% — but the quarter's real story was the backlog: contracts signed but not yet delivered (RPO) exploded 359% to $455B, while net income stayed flat at $2.9B as cloud delivery costs surged.

segments.name: Cloud
segments.note: Cloud infrastructure (OCI) and cloud applications (SaaS) — now 48% of all revenue. MultiCloud database revenue from Amazon, Google and Microsoft grew 1,529%.

segments.name: Software
segments.note: Traditional software licenses and support — shrinking slightly as customers migrate to the cloud.

segments.name: Services
segments.note: Consulting and support services that help customers run Oracle products.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building the cloud platform and the database software — up 8% YoY.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — finance, legal and the back office, up 5% YoY.

opex.name: Amortization of intangible assets
opex.note: Writing down the value of past acquisitions over time — a non-cash charge, down 33% YoY.

opex.name: Restructuring and other
opex.note: Restructuring charges of $402M — more than five times a year ago — plus $13M of acquisition-related costs.

follow100Note: Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: The backlog exploded
takeaways.text: Remaining performance obligations — contracts signed but not yet delivered — rose 359% in a year to $455B after four multi-billion-dollar contracts were signed in the quarter. Oracle expects cloud infrastructure revenue to grow 77% this fiscal year.

takeaways.title: Cloud is nearly half the company
takeaways.text: Cloud revenue rose 28% to $7.2B — 48% of all revenue — while traditional software shrank 1%. MultiCloud database revenue, from running Oracle databases inside Amazon, Google and Microsoft clouds, grew 1,529%.

takeaways.title: Profit flat while building
takeaways.text: Net income was $2.93B, unchanged from a year ago: cloud delivery costs jumped 39% and restructuring charges hit $402M as Oracle races to build AI data-center capacity. Non-GAAP EPS was $1.47.

oneTimers: Restructuring charges of $402M — more than five times the $73M of a year ago — sit inside operating expenses.
otherDetail: Interest expense of $923M on Oracle's growing debt pile, partly offset by $73M of non-operating income, net.
footerNote: Oracle reports its delivery costs as 'Cloud and software', 'Hardware' and 'Services' expense lines; those three are combined here as cost of revenue.
